opportunities.title: Funding for universities and research institutions

amount.raw: Minimum grant £100,000; usual grant range £250,000 – £1 million

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Research-intensive universities and research institutions in the UK undertaking internationally competitive research. Applications coordinated by the university Development Office.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants for new buildings, refurbishment work and major equipment to enable high-quality research, and sometimes to improve access and research libraries or public engagement with science. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for museums & galleries
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered or exempt charity (or equivalent) or local authority in the UK; fully accredited under the Museum Accreditation Scheme; holding a permanent collection of national significance.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants to improve the display and interpretation of nationally significant collections for the public, generally towards refurbishing or creating new galleries and occasionally education and learning spaces. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for historic buildings & landscapes
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered or exempt charity (or equivalent) or local authority in the UK managing sites of outstanding historic, architectural and cultural significance, open and accessible to the public, and listed at Grade I/II* or Scheduled Monument (England & Wales), Category A/B or Scheduled Monument (Scotland), Grade A/B+ or Scheduled Monument (Northern Ireland).
opportunities.summary: Capital grants for conservation and restoration work, interpretation, and education spaces at sites of outstanding historic, architectural and cultural significance with a clear emphasis on public access and engagement. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for libraries & archives
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered or exempt charity (or equivalent) or local authority in the UK; fully accredited under the Archive Service Accreditation Scheme; open and accessible to the public; holding a permanent collection of national significance.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants for collection storage facilities and research, education or interpretation spaces at libraries and archives caring for nationally significant collections with a clear emphasis on public access and engagement. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for performing arts organisations
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered or exempt charity (or equivalent) or local authority in the UK, focussed on professional performance with the performing arts constituting the vast majority of its activities.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants to improve training and education facilities for performing arts organisations, generally towards building or refurbishing these facilities and occasionally specialist equipment. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for public engagement with science organisations
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered or exempt charity (or equivalent), local authority or university in the UK displaying scientific or natural history collections of national significance; fully accredited under the Museum Accreditation Scheme if applicable.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants to improve public engagement with science through projects related to the history of science, generally towards refurbishing or creating new galleries and occasionally education and learning spaces. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for charities working with disability
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered or exempt charity (or equivalent) or local authority in the UK working with disability; if applicable, at least a 'Good' rating from a regulator such as CQC or Ofsted.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants to help people with disabilities live more independently, particularly projects focusing on training, employment and supported housing, especially helping young people transition from children's to adults' services. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for charities working in mental health
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered or exempt charity (or equivalent) or local authority in the UK working in mental health; if applicable, at least a 'Good' rating from a regulator such as CQC or Ofsted.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants for charities working in mental health, with an emphasis on projects focusing on training, employment and supported housing. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for charities working with older people
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered or exempt charity (or equivalent) or local authority in the UK providing care and services for older people, particularly those with a neurodegenerative condition or who are isolated; if applicable, at least a 'Good' rating from a regulator such as CQC.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants for new buildings, refurbishment work and equipment for organisations providing care and services for older people. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for hospices and palliative care organisations
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered charities or hospices operating within the NHS in the UK; if applicable, at least a 'Good' rating from a regulator such as CQC or equivalent.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants for new buildings, refurbishment work and equipment for places providing excellent care to patients and their families in hospices and palliative care organisations. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.

opportunities.title: Funding for special schools and colleges
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Registered or exempt charity (or equivalent) or local authority in the UK supporting special schools and colleges for children and young people with special educational needs; if applicable, at least a 'Good' rating from a regulator such as CQC or Ofsted.
opportunities.summary: Capital grants for projects supporting pupils at secondary level in special schools and colleges to develop skills to gain employment or live independently after school or college. Two-stage application process, two funding rounds per year.
